note: ADHD in unselected paediatric/adult patients treated with NET inhibitors (atomoxetine, viloxazine, centanafadine, dasotraline); the class's preclinical case was rat prefrontal microdialysis and monkey occupancy PET, while the SHR behavioural model was only ever tested retrospectively.
label: ADHD (NRIs)

engagement.model: Rat PFC microdialysis / ex vivo NET uptake
engagement.note: Atomoxetine raised prefrontal NE and DA 3-fold in rat microdialysis; the label cites ex vivo uptake studies as the mechanism basis.
engagement.short: Rat PFC NE and DA rose 3-fold
engagement.quote: In microdialysis studies, atomoxetine increased extracellular (EX) levels of NE in prefrontal cortex (PFC) 3-fold, but did not alter 5-HT(EX) levels.
engagement.judgement: Bymaster 2002 is a post-hoc mechanism paper (atomoxetine's ADHD efficacy was already known), so it opens the strip as untested. model_filed=true because Strattera label 12.1 states the mechanism was 'determined in ex vivo uptake and neurotransmitter depletion studies' (dailymed setid 309de576-c318-404a-bc15-660c2b1876fb). Same model reused for later class members: centanafadine (Bymaster 2012, doi:10.1002/syn.21538, PFC NE 375%/DA 300%), viloxazine (Yu 2020, doi:10.2147/JEP.S256586, 'moderate' NET inhibition), dasotraline (Schreiber 2022, doi:10.1016/j.biopha.2022.113359).

engagement.model: Rat PFC microdialysis / ex vivo NET uptake
engagement.note: [11C]MRB PET in 24 men: atomoxetine 25-100 mg blocked NET in most regions as the rat model said; magnitude unresolved.
engagement.short: Human PET: NET blocked at clinical doses
engagement.quote: While all three doses of ATX were found to block most regions, no significant differences between doses were found for any region, although the average percent change across subjects of the MBR did correlate with ATX dose.
engagement.reason: NET blocked in humans at clinical doses
engagement.judgement: Abstract-level read. Twenty-four male subjects in a tracer test/retest + blocking design (taken as healthy volunteers; the abstract does not say 'healthy'). Human NET blockade at 25-100 mg confirms the model's engagement claim in direction only: DVR fell just 17-31% and 'No relationship was found between DVR change and plasma ATX level', which the authors attribute to tracer signal-to-noise, not biology; they also note the 25 mg dose is below the paediatric therapeutic dose and 'there may be additional targets for ATX's therapeutic actions' (an efficacy caveat, not an engagement contradiction). comparison_stated=false: the source compares human NET distribution with nonhuman-primate localization, not the rat occupancy prediction. Registry: ClinicalTrials.gov search (intervention atomoxetine, sponsor Brookhaven) returned 0 records, so registry_date=null. Human target-engagement biomarker for a later class member exists but makes no model comparison: dasotraline plasma DHPG PK/PD in mixed healthy/ADHD subjects (Hopkins 2016, doi:10.1007/s40261-015-0358-7, NCT01692782, results first posted 2015-01-12).

dose.note: Monkey PET: atomoxetine occupied NET 38-82% dose-dependently; later monkey work predicted near-complete occupancy at clinical doses, never measured in patients.
dose.short: Monkey PET predicts saturation; never checked
dose.quote: After administration of atomoxetine, a dose-dependent occupancy from 38 to 82% was observed for various brain regions known to contain high densities of NET.
dose.judgement: The monkey model's dose prediction was stated explicitly but never tested in people. Gallezot 2011 (doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2010.09.040): ED50 0.13 mg/kg, 'much lower than the therapeutic dose of ATX in ADHD (1.0-1.5mg/kg)'. Takano 2009 (doi:10.1007/s00259-009-1118-9): Kd 16 ng/mL, 'clinical doses of atomoxetine would occupy NET almost completely'. Ding 2014 (doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2013.08.001, print 2014/epub 2013, monkey not human despite the title): '>90% of NET' at 300-600 ng/mL, 'This extrapolation assumes comparable free fraction of ATX in humans and non-human primates.' The only human occupancy study (Logan 2007, above) predates these, found no dose or plasma relationship and only 17-31% DVR change, and could not resolve magnitude; so the occupancy target is unverified rather than confirmed or contradicted. Atomoxetine's clinical dose (1.2 mg/kg) was set by empirical dose-ranging (label 14.1 Study 1), not by any model. model_filed=false: the label does not cite monkey PET.

efficacy.note: Atomoxetine improved Morris water-maze learning in SHR; a retrospective test of an approved drug, not a prediction.
efficacy.quote: The results indicated that atomoxetine significantly ameliorated performance in the Morris water maze, consistent with its histamine-enhancing profile.
efficacy.judgement: Earliest NRI-in-SHR paper found with a PubMed search on atomoxetine AND 'spontaneously hypertensive rat' (16 hits); earlier papers using only the abbreviation SHR may exist. Kept as untested rather than 'same' because the source makes a mechanism claim (histamine), not a prediction-vs-patient comparison. Note that no NRI pivotal preclinical paper used the SHR: centanafadine's used the neonatal 6-OHDA-lesioned juvenile rat (Bymaster 2012, doi:10.1002/syn.21538), and atomoxetine's used microdialysis only; the SHR is scored here because it is the field's standard ADHD efficacy model and the only one with a published patient comparison for this class.

efficacy.note: In SHR five-choice task atomoxetine had no effect on attention or impulsivity; authors conclude the SHR may lack predictive validity.
efficacy.short: SHR misses atomoxetine; lacks predictive validity
efficacy.quote: Furthermore, they suggest that the SHR may lack predictive validity and further investigation is needed to optimise use of this model.
efficacy.reason: SHR null for an effective drug
efficacy.judgement: Abstract-level read. 'There were no significant effects of atomoxetine on accuracy once multiple comparisons were taken into consideration' and no effect on premature responding; the authors themselves set this against atomoxetine's clinical use and question the model's predictive validity (comparison_stated=true; the patient side is atomoxetine's established efficacy, not new patient data). Corroborated by Turner 2013 (doi:10.1016/j.bbr.2012.12.025): oral atomoxetine 0.15-0.3 mg/kg had 'no effect ... on locomotor activity' and 'no effects on impulsivity' in SHR. The SHR literature is mixed (positive learning effects in Liu 2008 and a trimethyltin/SHR study, doi:10.1016/j.ejphar.2012.02.045), but a null for an effective drug on the core ADHD domains is a wrong prediction and contra overrides. Dasotraline: no SHR or other behavioural ADHD-model data were published for it; its preclinical profile (Schreiber 2022) appeared after the clinical program and reports only microdialysis/occupancy. No model flagged its discontinuation, and the discontinuation was not a clean efficacy failure: adult 8 mg positive (Koblan 2015, doi:10.1038/npp.2015.124, NCT01692782, results posted 2015-01-12), adult 4/6 mg negative (Adler 2021, doi:10.1097/YIC.0000000000000333, NCT02276209, no results posted), paediatric 4 mg positive (Findling 2019, doi:10.1089/cap.2018.0083, NCT02428088, no results posted), classroom 2 mg positive (2022, NCT03231800, results posted 2020-06-24). A primary source for the 2018 complete-response letter and 2020 discontinuation was not retrieved.

safety.model: Rat microdialysis (striatal/accumbens DA) + rat/monkey drug discrimination
safety.note: Rat microdialysis: no striatal or accumbens dopamine rise, so atomoxetine should lack motoric and drug-abuse liabilities.
safety.short: No accumbens DA, so no abuse
safety.quote: In contrast to methylphenidate, atomoxetine did not increase DA in striatum or nucleus accumbens, suggesting it would not have motoric or drug abuse liabilities.
safety.judgement: The one explicit safety prediction the class's preclinical package made was low abuse liability. The same reasoning was reused for dasotraline (baboon SPECT/striatal microdialysis, Schreiber 2022) and tested in recreational stimulant users (Koblan 2015, doi:10.1016/j.drugalcdep.2015.10.029: no drug-liking difference from placebo), again without a stated model comparison.

safety.model: Rat microdialysis (striatal/accumbens DA) + rat/monkey drug discrimination
safety.note: Label sets rat/monkey drug-discrimination data beside a human abuse-potential study: no stimulant or euphoriant properties; not scheduled.
safety.quote: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, abuse-potential study in adults that compared effects of STRATTERA and placebo, STRATTERA was not associated with stimulant or euphoriant properties.
safety.judgement: Label section 9.2 (read in the 6/2026 revision) carries both halves: the human abuse-potential study and 'Drug discrimination studies in rats and monkeys showed inconsistent stimulus generalization between atomoxetine and cocaine.' Year is set to the 2002 approval because the study is a pre-approval NDA study and atomoxetine was never scheduled; the original 2002 label could not be read (FDA's s000 link now serves the 2026 label; the 2003 PDF is the patient leaflet), so the date of this wording is unverified - flag for the maintainers. Subjects left null: the label says only 'adults' (the published study was in light drug users, not patients). The animal half is equivocal ('inconsistent'), so source_calls_it=null.

safety.model: Animal toxicology (rat, mouse, rabbit; juvenile rat)
safety.note: Boxed warning: suicidal ideation 0.4% vs 0% in pooled paediatric trials; no animal study addressed it.
safety.quote: STRATTERA increased the risk of suicidal ideation in pediatric patients aged 6 years of age and older with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in short-term studies.
safety.judgement: Scored contra under the brief's '(or its silence)' clause, as in the ad-amyloid example: the animal package (label 8.4 juvenile rat study with 'no effects on learning and memory tests'; 13.1 carcinogenicity/genotoxicity/fertility; 8.1 rabbit and rat reproduction) made no prediction about suicidality, and a boxed warning followed. Date from FDA approval letter NDA 21-411/S-014, signed 11/8/2005: 'This supplemental new drug application provides for the addition of a black box and other labeling changes regarding suicidality and Strattera' (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2005/021411s014ltr.pdf). Quote is from the 6/2026 label. Caveat for re-scoring: the signal is small (5/1,357 vs 0/851, no suicides, not seen in adults) and class-like for antidepressant-type drugs; maintainers who do not count silence should drop this entry and leave the cell at 'same'. Other unmodelled harms in the same vein: severe liver injury (postmarketing, label 5.2) and dasotraline psychosis-related AEs in 7/219 children (Findling 2019).
